definitions: A specific form of buttress composed of an arch that extends from the upper part of a wall to a pier, typically forming an open space beneath the arch.
An architectural support structure commonly found in Gothic cathedrals, designed to counteract the outward thrust of the walls and vaults.
examples: The cathedral's flying buttresses allowed for taller walls and larger windows.
Engineers studied the mechanics of the flying buttress.
The flying buttress is a hallmark of Gothic architecture.
